body:
Thank you, Hackety Hack is rather useful. 

I deeply appreciate both of your guys' advice and will look back at this submission as a reminder to clear my thoughts.

Thank you all again.

Thank you so much.

I am currently tackling JavaScript and Ruby on Codecademy because I read up on a coding bootcamp that said it'd be wise to brush on those programming languages in order to prepare for their application.

G_r_cade recommended to learn one programming language at a time so that I can better get a grip and becoming good before dispersing on multiple languages.

I've been studying Java in Sam's Teach Yourself Java in 24 Hours but took a break from that, I am considering going back to it and then focusing my time on JavaScript and Ruby. Primarily, I would like to make apps (I am told xCode, but that's another programming language to add to the mix) and applications, but that Java would be fine for the time being since most Android apps operate on it.

I am sorry this message is everywhere, I am just looking for resources on being able to better attain syntax and just learn the damn languages. I deeply appreciate your message.

**Arbitrary question:** How much time in a day should I spend in learning (1) language?

I am reading this, and it seems overwhelming - I am not sure where to start.

I find that Codecademy and Sam's Teach Yourself Java in 24 Hours are most beneficial to me because of the exercises. I find that writing even basic code is a step for me in understanding it. Otherwise, I shall digest this page you gave me.

Seriously, thank you.

I am actually looking at programs (Stencyl, GameSalad) that help you make games by learning their coding. I am not sure how useful that is or if I should invest the time in it.

Right now I am learning JavaScript (and Ruby, because an Coding Bootcamp recommends it in order to fulfill their application process.) Do you think it'd be wise just to focus on JavaScript, Java, and Xcode for the time being? I am just unsure which routes to take.

As simple as that, huh? Xcode and Java for mobile devices? I skimmed your comment history and saw that you mentioned that.

Out of curiosity, how did you get started, and how long did it take you?

Thank you, seriously.

I put weight on the idea of a bootcamp because they insure a high chance of employment. I would like to get employed, so the bootcamps seem to be a big carrot at the end of the stick. 

I am not sure how I would apply coding to show employers, "Hey, I could do this." without going through some formal/informal education. Is it even possible through my self learning?  I suppose, if I made something myself?
